label: extreme wide shot
text: extreme wide frame, subject barely legible in the landscape
note: Geography over subject. At 512x384 the subject may not survive; check before spending the render.

label: very wide shot
text: very wide frame, subject readable but small in the space

label: establishing wide
text: wide establishing frame, subject small in the space
note: EST is a role, not a size — it is a wide used first in a scene.

label: long shot
text: full body with space above and below
note: LS and WS are used interchangeably in most American shot lists.

label: full shot
text: full figure in frame, headroom above
note: Head to feet, frame edges close.

label: cowboy shot
note: Named for the framing that keeps a holstered gun in shot.

label: medium shot
text: framed from the waist up, subject dominant

label: wide close-up
text: head and a little shoulder, loose

label: close-up
text: close on the face, shoulders cropped

label: medium close shot
text: tighter than MCU, looser than CU

label: extreme close-up
text: extreme close-up, a single feature filling frame
note: Eyes, mouth, a hand. One feature only.

label: insert
text: insert on the object being handled, hands only
note: An object shot, not a face shot. Usually cut in, so the link is a cut.
